texts.facts: Petitioners who claim to have established business of distributing potable drinking water (RO) for needy public for Tiptur for affordable prices are calling in question seizure orders dated 09.03.2018 issued by third respondent as per Annexures-A to A5. 2. 3. Petitioners are claiming to be registered drinking water suppliers and said to have dug borewells, installed RO plants (Reverse Osmosis Potable Drinking Water Plants) for supplying clean drinking water and transporting the same to the needy public at very affordable prices. Petitioners have also obtained permission from the Town Municipality to install the R.O Plants as per Annexures-D to D4. Certificate issued by private testing laboratories certifying that water being supplied by the petitioners are potable and good for human consumption is produced as Annexures-E and E1 dated 16.09.2016 and 27.01.2017. 4. Notices came to be issued by third respondent calling upon the petitioners to close their units since they do not have ISI certification without which they cannot sell water. Said notices have been replied by petitioners as per Annexures-G to G3. It is the grievance of the petitioners that despite such reply given, third respondent - authority has proceeded to seize their units and as such, their fundamental right to carry on business is affected and public in need of clean drinking water are also being deprived of potable RO water at affordable price. Hence, they have sought for quashing of the impugned notices/orders. 5. Petitioners have filed affidavits on 26.06.2018 stating thereunder to the effect that they would file necessary application before the appropriate authority for grant of ISI certificate in respect of water to be sold by them within 14 days from the date of receipt of copy of the order and as such, they have prayed for six months time to obtain necessary permissions have also sought for direction to respondent to lift seizure of their units to enable them to run their business. 6. Further direction was also issued to the authorities to dispose of the applications which are pending for grant of certification within a time frame as indicated in the order dated 09.11.2012. 8.
texts.arguments: Learned Advocate appearing for petitioners have reiterated the grounds urged in the writ petitions. 7. Division Bench of this Court of which Aravind Kumar J was a member, in the case of LOCHAMESH B. HUGAR vs UNION OF INDIA, MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE DEPARTMENT AND OTHERS reported in ILR 2013 KAR 306 has held that Central Government Madhu B M vs State Of Karnataka on 27 June, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42738504/ 3 having brought in Food, Safety and Standards (Prohibition and Restriction on Sale) Regulations, 2011 which mandates sale of packaged drinking water is notified except under BIS certification and same having come into effect from 05.08.2011 had directed respondent - authorities to take all necessary steps to prohibit, prevent the manufacture or sale of packaged drinking water without certification from the Bureau of Indian Standards. cannot be heard to contend that they need not obtain BIS certification.
